scalesUsed.notes: F - G - A - Bb - C - D - E - F
scalesUsed.application: Entire harmonic framework; the song uses only the I and II (or V of Bb) chords from this key
Melodic vocal phrases and Lindsey Buckingham's lead guitar embellishments

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Ionian (Major) with a hypnotic, ambiguous quality created by the two-chord oscillation between F and G

mainProgression.description: A mesmerizing two-chord vamp alternating between F major and G major. The G functions as a secondary dominant (V/V) or simply as a major II chord, creating an open, unresolved quality that gives the song its dreamy, hypnotic character.

sectionProgressions.description: Repeating two-chord vamp providing a floating, hypnotic bed for Stevie Nicks' vocal melody
Same two-chord pattern as the verse with the 'Thunder only happens when it's raining' vocal hook adding melodic distinction
Lindsey Buckingham adds melodic guitar fills over the same chord vamp, using single-note lines from F major pentatonic

harmonicFunction: F (I) - Tonic chord, the warm and stable home base of the song
G (II) - Major supertonic chord, functioning as either a borrowed chord or V/V, creating gentle tension and forward motion before resolving back to F
The two-chord oscillation creates a sense of endless motion without full resolution, perfectly matching the song's themes of uncertainty and longing

techniques.name: Arpeggio Picking Pattern
techniques.description: A flowing arpeggiated picking pattern that breaks the F and G chords into individual notes rather than strumming, creating the dreamy, ethereal texture that defines the song

notes: F: 1-3-3-2-1-1 (standard F barre) or X-X-3-2-1-1 (simplified)
G: 3-2-0-0-0-3 (standard open G shape)
Pick each string individually in ascending then descending order
Use a combination of thumb (bass strings) and fingers (treble strings)
Alternatively, use a pick with a smooth, flowing down-up sweep across the strings
Let each note ring into the next for a harp-like quality
sequence: Pick the bass note (1st fret low E or 3rd fret A string) with thumb or downstroke
Roll through the remaining strings ascending: D, G, B, high E
Reverse the direction descending through the same strings
Transition to G chord and repeat the same picking pattern
Maintain smooth, flowing motion throughout the pattern
tips: Keep the picking hand relaxed and fluid - this should feel effortless
Allow generous sustain on each note; don't rush through the arpeggios
Practice the pattern on just one chord until it becomes second nature
A clean tone with slight reverb enhances the dreamy picked quality
The tempo is 120 BPM but the feel should be unhurried and flowing

techniques.name: Clean Tone Chord Voicings
techniques.description: Using full, ringing open chord voicings with a crystal-clear clean tone to achieve the warm, spacious sound that characterizes the Rumours-era Fleetwood Mac guitar work

notes: G: 3-2-0-0-0-3 (full open G with 3rd-fret high E for brightness)
F: X-X-3-2-1-1 (simplified F for beginners) or 1-3-3-2-1-1 (full barre)
Fmaj7: X-X-3-2-1-0 (alternative voicing adding dreamy seventh color)
Each chord should ring clearly with no muted or buzzing strings
Press just hard enough for clean tone - avoid squeezing the neck
sequence: Form the F chord shape ensuring all fretted notes ring clearly
Strum or pick the chord with a gentle, even stroke
Hold the chord for two beats, letting it sustain fully
Cleanly transition to the G chord on beat 3
Allow G to ring for two beats before returning to F
Repeat the cycle throughout the song
tips: The simplified F voicing (X-X-3-2-1-1) works perfectly for this song
Try the Fmaj7 voicing for an even dreamier quality
Ensure each string rings clearly by checking individual string sounds
The clean tone does not hide mistakes, so chord clarity is essential
Less is more - simple, clear chords create more impact than complex voicings

techniques.name: Two-Chord Song Dynamics
techniques.description: Creating musical interest and dynamic variation within a two-chord structure through subtle changes in picking intensity, voicing, and rhythmic feel across different song sections

notes: Verse: gentle arpeggiated picking at moderate volume (mp)
Chorus: slightly increased picking intensity and fuller voicings (mf)
Interlude: mix of arpeggios with occasional light strums
Vary picking position (closer to bridge for brightness, toward neck for warmth)
Add slight rhythmic variations to prevent monotony
Buckingham's approach: add single-note melodic fills between chord changes
sequence: Start the verse with soft, delicate arpeggiated picking
Introduce slightly fuller picking for the pre-chorus build
Open up to moderate intensity for the chorus vocal sections
Return to gentle picking for the next verse
Add small melodic fills during instrumental breaks
The overall dynamic arc should be subtle but clearly felt
tips: With only two chords, dynamics become your primary tool for expression
Think of each section as having its own personality within the same chord framework
Small changes have a large effect in a sparse arrangement
Listen to the original recording for how Buckingham varies his approach across sections
Resist the urge to add complexity - the simplicity is what makes this song work

sections.name: Intro
sections.description: Gentle, hypnotic opening establishing the two-chord vamp with soft arpeggiated picking over the bass and drum groove
notes: Establish the arpeggiated picking pattern from the very first beat
The bass and drums set the groove while guitar floats on top
Keep picking soft and delicate for the intro atmosphere
Let each arpeggio note ring into the next for full sustain

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: Flowing verse section with the two-chord vamp supporting Stevie Nicks' smooth vocal delivery about heartbreak and resilience
notes: Maintain consistent gentle picking beneath the vocal melody
The guitar should support, not compete with, the vocals
Each chord receives roughly two beats in the alternating pattern
The hypnotic repetition of F-G creates the song's mesmeric quality

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The memorable 'Thunder only happens when itthe signature chorus with slightly increased intensity while maintaining the same harmonic foundation
notes: Slightly increased picking or strumming intensity for the chorus
The vocal melody creates the distinction between verse and chorus, not the chords
Allow a touch more volume to lift the chorus emotionally
The same F-G alternation continues but with more energy in the delivery

sections.name: Instrumental Break
sections.description: Lindsey Buckingham's melodic guitar fills and single-note lines floating over the two-chord vamp during the instrumental section
notes: Buckingham adds tasteful single-note fills from F major pentatonic
The rhythm continues the arpeggiated pattern underneath
Lead lines are sparse and melodic, not flashy
This section demonstrates how melody can create interest within a simple harmony

sections.name: Outro
sections.description: Gradual fadeout on the repeating F-G vamp with the full band maintaining the hypnotic groove until the song dissolves
notes: Maintain the arpeggiated pattern consistently through the fade
The repeating two-chord vamp continues hypnotically to the end
Vocals and instrumentation fade gradually while guitar keeps steady
The song ends as it began - with the simple, eternal F-G oscillation

guitar.recommended: Fender Stratocaster or similar single-coil electric guitar
guitar.pickup: Neck pickup or middle position for warm, clean tone with smooth high end

amp.recommended: Fender Twin Reverb for pristine clean headroom
alternatives: Any clean-channel amplifier with good headroom

effects.distortion: None - pristine clean tone is essential
effects.reverb: Medium spring or plate reverb for spaciousness and depth
effects.other: Optional light chorus pedal for added shimmer. Compression can help even out arpeggiated picking volume. Keep effects minimal for authenticity.

beginner.focus: Learn the two chord shapes and basic arpeggiated picking pattern
steps: Master the open G chord shape (3-2-0-0-0-3)
Learn the simplified F chord (X-X-3-2-1-1) or Fmaj7 (X-X-3-2-1-0)
Practice transitioning cleanly between F and G at slow tempo
Add a basic arpeggiated picking pattern on each chord

intermediate.focus: Develop the flowing arpeggio pattern and play through the full song structure
steps: Learn the full F barre chord (1-3-3-2-1-1) if not already known
Practice the arpeggiated picking pattern at 120 BPM with a metronome
Play through the entire song with correct section dynamics
Add subtle variations in picking intensity between verse and chorus

advanced.focus: Add melodic fills, dynamic nuance, and sing along while picking
steps: Learn Buckingham-style single-note fills from F major pentatonic
Incorporate lead melodies over the arpeggiated pattern during instrumental sections
Practice singing while maintaining the picking pattern
Develop subtle dynamic variations to create interest within the two-chord structure
advanced.timeEstimate: 3-5 weeks for polished performance with fills

commonMistakes: Playing too loudly or aggressively - this song requires a gentle touch
Rushing the tempo because the two-chord pattern feels deceptively simple
Not allowing notes to sustain and ring into each other during arpeggios
Adding too many embellishments and losing the song's hypnotic simplicity
practiceRoutine: Warm up with arpeggiated picking on the G chord for 3 minutes (focus on smooth, even tone)
Practice the F to G transition repeatedly, ensuring no break in the picking pattern
Play the two-chord vamp for 5 minutes straight at 120 BPM, building consistency
Work on dynamic variation: 2 minutes soft, 2 minutes louder, 2 minutes soft again
Play through the complete song structure with the original recording
focusAreas: Even, flowing arpeggiated picking with consistent volume across strings
Smooth chord transitions without breaking the picking pattern
Dynamic control within a minimal harmonic framework
Clean tone quality with no buzzing or muted strings
metronomeWork: Start at 80 BPM with the arpeggiated pattern on a single chord
Practice chord transitions at 80 BPM, increasing by 10 BPM increments
Reach 120 BPM (song tempo) with smooth, consistent arpeggios
Practice at 120 BPM for sustained periods (5-10 minutes) to build consistency
